title: Prion diseases and rapidly progressive dementia

steps.tx: Sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease is a rapidly progressive dementia with **stimulus sensitive myoclonus** that ends in **akinetic mutism** and death, usually within 1 year of onset. It strikes about 1 per million each year, typically in later life, with men and women affected equally. Most cases are **sporadic** with no identifiable source. No case has ever remitted.

steps.tx: Most cases are **sporadic**, with no identifiable source, while a minority are **genetic** with PRNP mutations or **acquired** through variant disease from infected beef, historical kuru, and rare iatrogenic spread through dura grafts, corneal transplant, depth electrodes or cadaveric growth hormone. Genetic forms show autosomal dominant inheritance. Age in later life is the peak window.

steps.tx: The normal prion protein, **PrPc**, misfolds into the abnormal **PrPSc** form, swapping alpha helical structure for **beta pleated sheet**. Each misfolded molecule templates the conversion of its healthy neighbours, so infectivity spreads without any nucleic acid. Accumulating PrPSc kills neurons and astrocytes, leaving **spongiform vacuolation** and gliosis with strikingly no inflammation. Genotype at a key codon plus prion fragment type 1 or 2 defines the common sporadic subtypes.

steps.tx: About one third of patients report weeks of fatigue, depression, weight loss, or disturbed sleep before neurology declares itself. Then confusion with hallucinations, **cerebellar ataxia**, and distorted vision advance visibly week by week. The signature is **myoclonus** triggered by noise, light, or touch, sometimes only a fleeting startle response, while well formed seizures never belong to this illness. Decline continues into mutism, stupor, and coma.

steps.tx: The **Heidenhain variant** opens with cortical blindness and visual distortion, while the **Brownell-Oppenheimer variant** opens with progressive ataxia; both converge on dementia and myoclonus. Variant disease in the young instead begins with psychiatric and sensory symptoms and a longer course. Treatable mimics must be excluded first: **Hashimoto encephalopathy**, CNS vasculitis, CNS infection, lymphoma and autoimmune encephalitis can all pair dementia with myoclonus.

steps.tx: Brain **MRI with diffusion weighting** is the first test, showing restricted diffusion as a cortical ribbon plus **striatal hyperintensity** once disease is established. The EEG evolves from diffuse slowing to stereotyped **periodic sharp wave complexes**, often time locked to the jerks. CSF **RT-QuIC** seeding assay is the most specific confirmatory test, outperforming **14-3-3 protein**. Definite diagnosis still rests on brain histopathology with PrPSc immunostaining.

steps.tx: No drug halts prion disease, so care is **supportive and palliative** from the day of diagnosis. Standard precautions apply because casual contact carries no risk, yet instruments demand **prion grade decontamination** with specialist high temperature processing, since routine boiling, formalin and alcohol all fail. Affected patients must never donate organs, corneas or blood. Families with inherited disease need genetic counselling.

steps.tx: Modern criteria accept **RT-QuIC positivity** or characteristic MRI as the backbone of probable diagnosis during life, reserving biopsy for unresolved cases. Nasal mucosal brushing RT-QuIC and tonsil immunostaining in variant disease extend testing beyond lumbar puncture. No disease modifying therapy exists, so care stays **supportive**. National surveillance centres perform confirmatory testing free of charge and track iatrogenic exposures.

steps.tx: Late disease brings **aspiration pneumonia**, urinary incontinence and total immobility, with myoclonus sometimes persisting into coma. Sporadic disease kills within months from onset. Inherited forms run a longer course over several years with ataxia and dementia. Whatever the form, the trajectory is **invariably fatal**, and unusually prolonged survival should prompt diagnostic review.

steps.tx: **High yield for the exam:** incidence 1 per million with onset in later life; stimulus sensitive myoclonus plus periodic complexes; DWI cortical ribbon and striatal signal; RT-QuIC beats 14-3-3; P102L marks inherited GSS; iatrogenic spread via dura, cornea and growth hormone; specialist decontamination with donation ban.
steps.say: High yield for the exam: incidence is one per million with onset in later life, and stimulus sensitive myoclonus plus periodic complexes is the signature. Diffusion cortical ribbon and striatal signal is the imaging hallmark, and RT-QuIC is the best live test ahead of fourteen three three. P one hundred two L is the marker of inherited GSS. Iatrogenic spread via dura, cornea and growth hormone is the reason for the donation ban with specialist decontamination.
